title: His guitars: Stella, Martin and the Epiphone
summary: Rosenberg traces photos of round-hole flat-top guitars to the arch-top Epiphone; Bunn says he played whichever guitar sounded best.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: And at that time in the '30s maybe, when you were playing with the Spirits and with some of these record sessions, you were playing mostly Epiphone (UNINTELLIGIBLE)
Yeah. Uh-huh.
When did you switch to arch top guitar? I notice like the early stuff, really early stuff, you have a flat top, you know, with a round hole?
Yeah.
And then when did you switch to the Epiphone orchestra guitar?
I done that in -- oh, boy. Let's see, now. When I started playing the electric guitar, you say?
No. With the actual acoustic. Like I've seen a couple of pictures when you were with the Washboard Serenaders and in the really early Spirits pictures.
Well, I wasn't using no electric guitar then at all.
No, no. I mean even with the acoustic guitar, the very early stuff you have a round hole, you know, like a Martin style guitar?
Yes.
I think the earliest picture you have a Stella.
Yeah.
And then, later on, there's a picture of you with a Martin.
A Martin?
Yeah. And these were the round hole type of flat top.
Yeah.
But then, later on, in the --
And you saw that guitar?
I've seen a couple of pictures, yeah.
That I was playing on?
Yeah. I saw a picture of you with a Stella. It looks like a Stella, or maybe a Gibson, but I think it was a Stella.
Well, it could be.
In 1931, you know. Real early.
Yeah. It could be a Stella.
But then, by the time '37, '38, you had the Epiphone.
Yeah.
With the arched top.
Yeah.
I just wondered when you switched, if you can remember.
Well, any guitar I got ahold of I'd play.
I see.
See? I mean, I wouldn't look at the name of it.
Just check it out for the sound?
Just check it out for the sound.
Yeah.
The one that sounded the best, I just played.
Uh-huh. That's reasonable.
To me, yeah.
